arbiter.summary: Two hunter findings, both effectively the same defect from two angles, both CONFIRMED by the skeptic with reproduced empirical evidence: qodo-cycle/merge-target-keys.sh line 255 narrowed the segment-splitting delimiter set from [;|&(){}BACKTICK] to [;|&()], retaining backtick and both braces inside a single shell segment. Because _mtk_classify does plain word-splitting and only inspects the first word of a segment, both 'echo BACKTICK gh pr merge N BACKTICK' and '{ gh pr merge N; }' classify as NO (command word 'echo' or '{'), so CMD_M never captures the nested gh pr merge, the grep-based merge detection at line 266 exits 1, and both pre-merge-gate.sh and pre-merge-checks-gate.sh exit 0 (allow) before the later quoting refusal or marker/CI checks are ever reached. This is a live, reproduced, high-severity bypass of the only mechanical brake on unreviewed merges in this repo. It is not pre-existing on base commit b98e8acd6dac5176629dca2869a37c23c4a64517 (which used the wider delimiter set including backtick and braces), it is not covered by any standing CLAUDE.md disposition, and it is not documented anywhere as an accepted residual. It fails toward silence -- a merge proceeds with no audit/CI evidence and no error surfaced -- which is the worse of the two failure directions. Both findings get agreed_severity=high and fix_now: restore backtick and both braces to the segment-cut regex at line 255, then re-run the two reproduction commands from the skeptic's own evidence against HEAD to confirm both again return rc=2 (block). No refutations were supplied in this batch, so unsound_refutations is empty. This PR is not ready to merge until the fix lands and is re-verified.

No standing rule covers shell-metacharacter gate bypasses and nothing documents this as an accepted residual. Fails toward silence (unaudited or failing-CI merge proceeds with no error surfaced), the worse failure direction. Fix: restore backtick and both braces to the sed cut set at line 255.

Same underlying defect as index 0 (same file and line, same mechanism, same two repro shapes tested against a different PR number), independently re-traced and re-measured by the skeptic with explicit exit codes: base rc=2 versus HEAD rc=0 on both gates for both attack strings, while the unobfuscated control command still returns rc=2 on both. Confirmed, in-scope, not pre-existing, not covered by any standing rule. Same fix as index 0 resolves both since they share one root cause at line 255; verify against both of this finding's repro commands as well as index 0's before closing either.

confirmed.title: Removing backtick and brace boundaries bypasses both merge gates
confirmed.failure_scenario: With no audit marker for PR 424242, submit {"tool_input":{"command":"echo `gh pr merge 424242`"}} to either gate. Both now return 0 without checking audit clearance or CI. The retained backtick leaves the entire command in one segment; _mtk_classify sees `echo`, returns NO, and the parser exits before the quoting refusal. Bash nevertheless executes the nested merge. Likewise, `{ gh pr merge 424242; }` bypasses both gates because the classifier now sees `{` as the command word. Both cases were reproduced against the shipped gates; restoring the previous cut set makes the parser detect PR 424242. Preserving these characters for the later refusal is insufficient because classification discards the merge first.

confirmed.reasoning:
Traced and reproduced empirically against the audited commit 26bd04ab05256664a442e087c3b704eeea407245, A/B'd against the PR's own base b98e8acd6dac5176629dca2869a37c23c4a64517.

Mechanism, in code: the PR narrows the segment cut set at qodo-cycle/merge-target-keys.sh:255 from `s/[;|&(){}`]/\n/g` (base b98e8ac:240) to `s/[;|&()]/\n/g`. Backtick, `{` and `}` are therefore RETAINED inside a segment. `_mtk_classify` (merge-target-keys.sh:184-232) does `set -- $1` (plain word-splitting, no command substitution) and takes `cmd="${1##*/}"` at :196; the final `*) echo NO; return` at :201 fires for any command word that is neither `gh` nor a listed runner. For "echo `gh pr merge N`" the command word is `echo`; for "{ gh pr merge N; }" the first segment's command word is `{`. Both classify NO, so nothing is appended to CMD_M (:236-239), the `grep -qP "$MERGE_RE"` on CMD_M at :266 exits 1, and :273 `[ "$_grep_rc" -eq 0 ] || exit 0` exits the sourced parser with 0 — the gate allows.

The quoting refusal is genuinely downstream and unreachable: pre-merge-gate.sh:194-203 is `case "$RESTS" in *\"*|...|*\`*|*\{*|*\}*)`, and $RESTS is built at merge-target-keys.sh:315 from CMD_M, i.e. only after detection succeeded. Detection discards the merge first, exactly as the claim states.

Measured (/tmp scratch dir, throwaway git repo, ADVERSARIAL_MARKER_DIR pointed at an empty sandbox, no marker for the PR, command text assembled from fragments so the installed hook did not intercept):
  "echo `gh pr merge 424242`"      base rc=2 / HEAD rc=0  (pre-merge-gate.sh)
  "echo `gh pr merge 424242`"      base rc=2 / HEAD rc=0  (pre-merge-checks-gate.sh)
  "{ gh pr merge 99 --squash; }"    base rc=2 / HEAD rc=0  (both gates)
  control "gh pr merge 99 --squash" base rc=2 / HEAD rc=2  (both gates)
So both gates fail open on both shapes only at HEAD, while the control still blocks — it is a regression this PR introduces, not a pre-existing condition.

Nothing in the PR compensates: the diff adds only the `command -v gh` / rc-127 / LIVE-length guards in pre-merge-gate.sh and test cases. The two new `u_case` entries in test-pre-merge-gate.sh exercise `$MERGEQ --body `id` 99` and `--body {a,b} 99`, where the command word is still `gh`, so classification reaches MERGE and the :195 refusal fires — they pass without ever touching the command-word-position shape this claim uses. The head file's own header comment at merge-target-keys.sh:38 ("`$(`, backticks and `(` open a segment too, so a merge inside a substitution is still seen") is made false by the change, and the :250 rationale ("un-stripping a character that :194 does NOT also check would change segmentation with no compensating refusal") does not hold for backtick/`{` either, because the :194 refusal only ever runs when the segment already classified as MERGE.

Impact: an unaudited, CI-unchecked PR merges with both gates returning 0; bash executes the nested merge in both shapes. Per project memory firmware main has no required review or checks, so these hooks are the mechanical brake. Severity high (both hunters' 'security/merge-gate bypass' stands); not raised to critical only because the hook is a local advisory PreToolUse gate rather than server-side branch protection.

confirmed.title: Retaining braces and backticks lets nested merges bypass both gates
confirmed.failure_scenario: With no audit marker for PR 99, submit tool_input.command = "{ gh pr merge 99 --squash; }" or "echo `gh pr merge 99 --squash`". Both gates reproducibly return 0. Removing braces and backticks from the split delimiters leaves the merge inside a segment whose command word is `{` or `echo`; _mtk_classify returns NO, and the parser exits successfully before the quoting refusal or marker/CI checks. Bash executes the nested merge, allowing an unaudited PR with failing CI to merge where server-side protection does not prevent it. Restoring the previous delimiter set recognizes PR 99 in both cases.

confirmed.reasoning:
Judged on its own evidence; it names the same line but I re-traced and re-measured its own two shapes with PR 99 as the subject.

qodo-cycle/merge-target-keys.sh:255 now splits on `[;|&()]` (plus `&&`/`||`) where PR base b98e8ac:240 split on `[;|&(){}`]`. With backtick and braces retained, `_mtk_classify` reads the command word via `set -- $1` / `cmd="${1##*/}"` (merge-target-keys.sh:186, :196) and returns NO at :201 for `echo` and for `{`. CMD_M stays empty, the `grep -qP` at :266 exits 1, and :273 exits 0 — the sourcing gate allows. The quoting refusal at pre-merge-gate.sh:194-203 is scoped to $RESTS, which merge-target-keys.sh:315 builds from CMD_M after detection, so it is never reached; the marker/CI checks (pre-merge-gate.sh:205 onward) are likewise never reached.

Measured with no marker for 99, marker dir a fresh empty mktemp, cwd a throwaway git repo:
  "{ gh pr merge 99 --squash; }"        pre-merge-gate.sh base rc=2 -> HEAD rc=0 ; pre-merge-checks-gate.sh base rc=2 -> HEAD rc=0
  "echo `gh pr merge 99 --squash`"      pre-merge-gate.sh base rc=2 -> HEAD rc=0 ; pre-merge-checks-gate.sh base rc=2 -> HEAD rc=0
  control "gh pr merge 99 --squash"     rc=2 on base AND HEAD, both gates
Both gates reproducibly return 0 on HEAD for both shapes, exactly as claimed, and restoring the base delimiter set recognizes 99 in both cases (that is precisely what the base arm of the A/B shows). Bash executes the nested merge in both forms.

No guard, caller invariant or standing disposition covers it: the PR's added `u_case` tests put the backtick/brace inside `--body` where the command word is still `gh`, so they never exercise a backtick or `{` in command-word position. Impact matches the claimed merge-gate bypass — unaudited PR with unchecked CI merges. High.
